headline_marked: [[Tencent's Apache-licensed Hy3]] rivals GLM-5.2 at half the size, winning in search & tools
headline: Tencent's Apache-licensed Hy3 rivals GLM-5.2 at half the size, winning in search & tools
summary: Tencent's new 295B-parameter Hy3 MoE model is now Apache 2.0 licensed, making it accessible globally. It outperforms models 2-5x its size in agentic search and tool orchestration.
details: Tencent has released the full version of its Hy3 AI model under the permissive Apache 2.0 license, removing previous restrictions that limited its use in the EU, UK, and South Korea. This strategic move makes the powerful open-weight model globally accessible for enterprises.

Hy3 is a 295-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 21 billion active parameters per forward pass. The Apache 2.0 license marks a significant shift from its preview release, drawing immediate positive reaction from the open-model community.

Tencent positioned Hy3 for production use, emphasizing reliability metrics and deployment economics. The company conducted a blind human study with 270 experts, where Hy3 scored 2.67 against GLM-5.1's 2.51, showing advantages in frontend development, CI/CD, and data work.

While Hy3 trails GLM-5.2 in agentic coding benchmarks like SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench 2.1, this is expected given GLM-5.2's larger size (744B total, 40B active parameters). Hy3 operates with less than half the parameters and per-token compute of its coding rival.

Hy3 truly excels in agentic search, achieving 84.2 on BrowseComp and 91.0 on DeepSearchQA, competing with top proprietary models like Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5. It also leads the open field in tool orchestration (79.1 on MCP-Atlas) and long-context retrieval (73.4 on AA-LCR).

The model's strengths make it a strong open-weight choice for search-and-tool-heavy agent workloads. Tencent's internal testing provided most competitor numbers, a common practice that warrants independent verification.

headline_marked: [[AI golem Tilly Norwood reportedly 'starring']] in feature-length movie 'Misaligned'
headline: AI golem Tilly Norwood reportedly 'starring' in feature-length movie 'Misaligned'
summary: The film, titled "Misaligned," is described as a "coming-of-age story infused with existential AI chaos" set in the "Tillyverse," where Norwood seeks to become more human.
details: AI 'actor' Tilly Norwood is reportedly set to star in a feature-length movie titled 'Misaligned,' produced by Particle6 Productions. The film is described as a 'coming-of-age story infused with existential AI chaos' and is set in the 'Tillyverse'.

The plot involves Norwood's character attempting to become more human, encountering a 'seductive rogue bot from the dark web.' Particle6 CEO Eline van der Velden states the film will be 'funny, chaotic and self-aware — very Tilly'.

This would mark Particle6 Productions' first full-length feature, a significant step from their previous short-form AI marketing videos. The company also offers AI services for landscape generation and VFX to film studios.

Despite the announcement, the details remain fuzzy, and no human collaborators from the film industry have been officially announced. The production is suggested to be a hybrid, combining traditional filmmakers with AI specialists.

Skepticism surrounds the project, with some viewing Tilly Norwood as more of a 'ragebait machine' than a serious film industry innovation. Her initial introduction at the Zurich Film Festival reportedly stirred fear in Hollywood.

Particle6 previously responded to these fears with short videos that appeared to mock industry concerns. It remains to be seen if 'Misaligned' will actually be produced, or if the announcement serves primarily as a publicity stunt.
